stories.headline: Trump signs Arctic security pact with Denmark and Greenland, pledging two new US bases

key_facts.fact: Trump signed an agreement with Denmark and Greenland on Sept. 22 at the UN General Assembly aimed at strengthening Arctic and North Atlantic security, easing tensions over his repeated calls to annex the island.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump has signed an agreement with Denmark and Greenland aimed at strengthening Arctic and North Atlantic security, easing tensions over his repeated calls for Greenland to become part of the United States.

key_facts.fact: In his UN speech Trump said the US will 'immediately begin the process of developing a large military presence in the appropriate locations,' including 'building two very major military bases.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We will immediately begin the process of developing a large military presence in [the] appropriate locations," he said, including "building two very major military bases."

key_facts.fact: The trilateral ceremony was held at 10:30 a.m. ET with Danish PM Mette Frederiksen and Greenland PM Jens-Frederik Nielsen; the text of the agreement remained unpublished ahead of the signing.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump will meet Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen at 10:30 a.m. ET at the UN General Assembly in New York for the trilateral signing ceremony. ... The text remains unpublished ahead of Tuesday's signing.

key_facts.fact: Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said the deal places Arctic security under NATO's collective watch rather than leaving it to Washington and Copenhagen alone.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement "will be in a form where responsibility for security in the Arctic is not only Danish or American," Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen told national broadcaster TV2 on Sunday. He said that, to a large extent, "it would be NATO that looks after the Arctic."

key_facts.fact: Trump had posted that the deal gives the US 'permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland,' and that no adversary could base forces there without Washington's written approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said in a social media post on Friday the agreement gave the U.S. "permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," and that no U.S. adversary could have a base or military presence there without Washington's written approval.

key_facts.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio called it a 'historic agreement' that 'permanently guarantees U.S. security interests in the Arctic at zero cost to the U.S. taxpayer.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Thanks to President Trump's vision and leadership, this historic agreement permanently guarantees U.S. security interests in the Arctic at zero cost to the U.S. taxpayer," he said.

key_facts.fact: Frederiksen said the deal 'recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination'; it still needs parliamentary procedures to enter into force.
key_facts.excerpt: "An agreement that at the same time recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination." ... it would need to go through "necessary parliamentary procedures to enter into force."

stories.headline: Iran offers to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in seven days if the US lifts its port blockade

key_facts.fact: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Sept. 22 that Iran can reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US eases military pressure and lifts its blockade on Iranian ports.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran can reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Tehran delivered its latest proposal to Washington through mediators on Sept. 16; the official called the UN General Assembly 'a golden opportunity for the US to return to diplomacy.'
key_facts.excerpt: The Iranian official said details on an agreement to end hostilities with Washington can be discussed in New York via mediators, explaining that Tehran's proposal was delivered to the US via mediators on September 16th.

key_facts.fact: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian left Tehran for New York on Tuesday morning but will not meet Trump; it would be the first event both attend since Trump launched 'Operation Epic Fury' in February.
key_facts.excerpt: The event would be the first attended by Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian since Trump launched "Operation Epic Fury" against Iran in February, alongside Israel. ... A senior Iranian official said there were no plans for the two leaders to meet directly, but that Iran's delegation had full authority to revive talks.

key_facts.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US was open to speaking with the Iranians at the General Assembly 'especially if it has the prospects of leading to something positive.'
key_facts.excerpt: Secretary of State Marco Rubio told NBC's "Today" show the US was open to speaking with the Iranians, "especially if it has the prospects of leading to something positive and ultimately achieving the goal of what this is all about".

key_facts.fact: Trump was due to meet the leaders of all six Gulf Arab states on Sept. 22; on the table is a Qatari proposal for a common security architecture including Iran, which Tehran is reviewing.
key_facts.excerpt: On the table at the Gulf states' meeting with Trump is a Qatari proposal for a framework to bring Iran and the Arab Gulf states into a common security architecture, regional sources said. One source said Iran was reviewing the proposal.

key_facts.fact: Kyodo reported the initiative was approved by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and the Supreme National Security Council, and seeks an end to the port blockade and US operations around the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: The official said the initiative had been approved by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and the Supreme National Security Council. Iran is seeking an end to the blockade of its ports and US military operations related to the strait.

key_facts.fact: On Sunday Iran's military central command said it had been told the US was preparing to restart operations with regional support, warning of retaliation 'without limitations and considerations.'
key_facts.excerpt: On Sunday, Iran's military central command said it was informed the US was preparing to restart military operations with the support of regional countries, and warned this would lead to Tehran's retaliation "without limitations and considerations".

stories.headline: Brent slides below $100 as Saudi Gulf loadings surge — even as two more tankers are hit in Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell 3.4% to $100.34 a barrel on Sept. 21 and WTI dropped 4.5% to $95.78, their lowest closes since Sept. 8 and a fourth consecutive session of declines.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures fell 3.4% to $100.34 a barrel, and West Texas Intermediate dropped 4.5% to $95.78 a barrel, their lowest closes since Sept. 8.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Aramco loaded about 14 million barrels of crude onto seven supertankers inside the Gulf on Sunday after drone attacks shut its East-West Pipeline on Sept. 13.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Aramco loaded about 14 million barrels of crude oil on seven supertankers inside the Mideast Gulf on Sunday, data from TankerTrackers.com showed ... Drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its East-West Pipeline on September 13.

key_facts.fact: JPMorgan satellite data showed Saudi oil moving through Hormuz averaged 2.9 million barrels a day over six days, up from about 700,000 bpd in August.
key_facts.excerpt: JP Morgan analysts said in a September 18 note that satellite data indicated Saudi oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 2.9 million barrels per day over the past six days, up from just 700,000 bpd in August.

key_facts.fact: Two more tankers were struck while transiting Hormuz on Sept. 21 — one inbound vessel hit by an unknown projectile injuring two crew, and an outbound LPG tanker hit by projectile debris.
key_facts.excerpt: UK Maritime Trade Operations said Monday that military authorities reported an inbound tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the strait. Two crew members suffered minor injuries ... Hours later, UKMTO issued a second warning involving an LPG tanker making an outbound transit.

key_facts.fact: At least five tanker attacks or security incidents have been reported in the strait since Sept. 16, and the Joint Maritime Information Center rates the threat level SEVERE.
key_facts.excerpt: That brings the number of reported attacks or security incidents involving tankers in the strait to at least five since Sept. 16. ... JMIC continues to rate the threat level in the Strait of Hormuz as SEVERE.

key_facts.fact: Only 17 commodity vessels were visible transiting Hormuz over the weekend, down from 37 a week earlier and against roughly 125 per day before the war.
key_facts.excerpt: Just 17 commodity vessels were visible transiting the strait over the weekend, down from 37 a week earlier and compared with roughly 125 vessels per day before the war, according to Kpler data reported by Reuters.

key_facts.fact: Around 15% of the world's very large crude carrier fleet is now parked off Oman for ship-to-ship transfers, pushing tanker freight rates sharply higher.
key_facts.excerpt: Around 15% of the global fleet of very large crude carriers is now off Oman, according to Clarksons Research. Tanker freight rates have climbed sharply as vessels are tied up in shuttle operations and longer voyages.

key_facts.fact: Oil is up more than 65% in 2026 and US diesel hit a fresh high above $6.50 a gallon; Brent was around $72 in late February before the Iran war began.
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices are up more than 65% this year, while diesel remains at the center of the global fuels crunch, reaching a fresh high above $6.50 a gallon at U.S. pumps.

stories.headline: United Russia takes 57.5% in Russia's first wartime Duma election, held under record drone attack

key_facts.fact: Putin-backed United Russia was on course to dominate the parliamentary election with 57.5% of the vote after more than 71% of ballots were counted.
key_facts.excerpt: Putin-backed United Russia was on course to dominate Russia's parliamentary election, winning 57.5% of the vote with more than 71% of ballots counted.

key_facts.fact: It was the first election to the 450-seat State Duma since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, with turnout near 57% and 111 million eligible voters.
key_facts.excerpt: The vote, which is all but certain to cement the Kremlin's dominance, began on Friday for 111 million eligible voters and ended Sunday.

key_facts.fact: The liberal Yabloko party — the only registered party opposing the war — was barred from standing by Russia's top court, and balloting included four illegally annexed Ukrainian regions plus Crimea.
key_facts.excerpt: The liberal Yabloko party was the only registered party to oppose the war in Ukraine, but the country's top court barred it from standing. ... The balloting included residents of four Ukrainian regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the war began.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine launched what Moscow called the largest drone attack of the war on the final day of voting; Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 1,600 drones were downed, 450 of them approaching Moscow.
key_facts.excerpt: "The biggest attack by enemy drones has been repelled. Since yesterday, more than 1,600 drones have been shot down across all fronts. Of these, 450 were approaching Moscow," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.

key_facts.fact: The strikes killed three people in the Moscow region and two in the Russian-held part of Kherson, including an election official, and hit Moscow's oil refinery.
key_facts.excerpt: The drone strikes killed three people in the Moscow region and two more in the Russian-held part of Ukraine's Kherson region, including an election official, according to the region's governor and the election commission.

key_facts.fact: Russia's defence ministry said it would 'continue and intensify' high-accuracy strikes on military targets in Kyiv; Russian drones hit Zaporizhzhia on Monday, wounding five.
key_facts.excerpt: "In response to the Kyiv regime's attacks on civilian targets within Russia, the Russian army will continue and intensify its high-accuracy strikes against military targets in Kyiv," the Russian defence ministry said.

key_facts.fact: Moscow said it downed 244 Ukrainian drones overnight into Monday, while Ukraine's air force said it shot down or suppressed 148 Russian drones.
key_facts.excerpt: The Russian Defense Ministry said Monday that its air defenses overnight downed 244 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions and the waters of the Black Sea. Meanwhile, Ukraine's air force said Monday it shot down or suppressed 148 Russian drones in an overnight attack.

stories.headline: Binance buys a $100M stake in Circle and signs a five-year deal to push USDC in emerging markets

key_facts.fact: Circle and Binance announced on Sept. 22 a new five-year commercial agreement to expand USDC access across emerging markets, alongside a $100 million strategic equity investment by Binance in Circle.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies have entered into a new, five-year commercial agreement focused on expanding USDC access across emerging markets. Further, Binance has made a $100 million strategic equity investment in Circle.

key_facts.fact: The private placement closed Sept. 17: Binance acquired 1.24 million Class A shares at $80.84 each, a 5% discount to market, with a lockup of up to two years but retained voting rights.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance bought $100 million in Circle shares through a private placement that closed Sept. 17, acquiring 1.24 million shares at $80.84 each. Binance generally cannot sell, transfer or hedge the shares for up to two years, though it retains voting rights.

key_facts.fact: Under the deal Circle will pay Binance a monthly incentive fee calculated as a percentage of USDC held through Circle's Modular Smart Contract Wallet service, replacing earlier agreements from November 2024 and August 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Circle agreed to pay Binance a monthly incentive fee calculated as a percentage of the USDC held through Circle's Modular Smart Contract Wallet service ... The new arrangement replaces Circle and Binance's earlier USDC deals from November 2024 and August 2025.

key_facts.fact: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the $100 million investment and five-year commitment 'represent long-duration conviction' and that 'a stable, trusted digital dollar should not be a privilege.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Our $100 million investment and five-year commitment represent long-duration conviction," said Richard Teng, co-CEO of Binance. "A stable, trusted digital dollar should not be a privilege–it should be available to anyone with a phone."

key_facts.fact: The agreement signals Circle's push to expand USDC beyond its historically US-focused base and compete more directly with Tether in international crypto markets.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement signals a push to expand USDC beyond its historically U.S.-focused base and compete more directly with stablecoin giant Tether in international crypto markets.

key_facts.fact: Circle stock briefly jumped more than 3% on Tuesday before slipping to a fractional decline; the news lands as the DOJ and the Manhattan US attorney reportedly probe Binance over alleged Iran-sanctions violations.
key_facts.excerpt: News of the deal comes as the Justice Department and the Manhattan U.S. attorney's office reportedly probe Binance over alleged Iran-sanctions violations. Circle stock briefly jumped more than 3% Tuesday, before settling back into a fractional decline during morning…

stories.headline: Boehringer Ingelheim commits up to $1B to Envisagenics' RNA-splicing cancer targets

key_facts.fact: Boehringer Ingelheim announced on Sept. 22 a partnership with New York-based Envisagenics worth up to more than $1 billion, covering an undisclosed upfront, research funding, option fees and development, regulatory and commercial milestones.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal could put Boehringer on the hook for up to more than $1 billion, including an unspecified upfront commitment, research funding, option fees and development, regulatory and commercial milestones. New York–based Envisagenics is also eligible for royalties on product sales, according to a Tuesday announcement.

key_facts.fact: Envisagenics' platform uses AI to screen for cancer-specific RNA splicing alterations, which the companies call 'one of the last largely untapped sources' of therapeutic targets.
key_facts.excerpt: Envisagenics' platform makes use of AI to screen and detect cancer-specific RNA alterations ... a particular molecular alteration in cancer that the companies claim is "one of the last largely untapped sources" of potential therapeutic targets.

key_facts.fact: Boehringer will target the identified splicing events with multi-specific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates and T cell engagers, and can take exclusive licences on selected targets.
key_facts.excerpt: Boehringer will have the option to secure an exclusive license for certain targets and will "take the lead and full responsibility for modality selection, development and commercialization of the resulting therapeutic."

key_facts.fact: Envisagenics CEO Maria Pineda said Boehringer is 'focused on aggressive solid tumors with significant unmet need and limited treatment options' and that the partners will work closely on target validation.
key_facts.excerpt: Pineda noted that Boehringer is "focused on aggressive solid tumors with significant unmet need and limited treatment options."

key_facts.fact: The deal joins a wave of RNA-splicing bets in pharma: Merck KGaA put more than $2 billion of potential deal value behind Skyhawk Therapeutics for neurological conditions.
key_facts.excerpt: In August last year, Merck KGaA partnered with Skyhawk to advance these RNA modulators for unspecified neurological conditions. The German pharma has put over $2 billion in potential deal value on the line for the agreement.

sources.title: Boehringer Ingelheim bets up to $1B in AI-centered solid tumor collab with Envisagenics

stories.headline: Nigeria's central bank cuts rates 350bp to 23%, breaking with a hawkish turn elsewhere

key_facts.fact: The Central Bank of Nigeria cut its Monetary Policy Rate by 350 basis points to 23% from 26.5% on Sept. 22, its second reduction of 2026, at the conclusion of the 307th MPC meeting in Abuja.
key_facts.excerpt: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) on Tuesday cut its benchmark interest rate by 350 basis points to 23 per cent from 26.5 per cent, marking its second rate reduction in 2026 ... The decision was taken at the conclusion of the 307th Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting held on September 22, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The rate returns to the 23% range for the first time since February 2024; the Cash Reserve Requirement stays at 45% for deposit money banks and 16% for merchant banks, and the standing facilities corridor was recalibrated to +50/-300 basis points.
key_facts.excerpt: The rate has returned to the 23% range for the first time since February 2024 as inflation continues to moderate. The apex bank retained CRR at 45% for deposit money banks and 16% for merchant banks. ... the Standing Facilities Corridor was recalibrated to +50/-300 basis points around the MPR.

key_facts.fact: Headline inflation fell to 15.39% in August from 15.43% in July and 23.14% a year earlier, with food inflation down to 19.57% year-on-year.
key_facts.excerpt: Nigeria's headline inflation fell to 15.39% in August from 15.43% in July, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Food inflation also declined to 19.57% year-on-year in August.

key_facts.fact: The MPC flagged external risks including escalating global tariffs and Middle East geopolitical tensions that could raise imported inflation and disrupt commodity markets.
key_facts.excerpt: The Committee also identified growing external risks to Nigeria's inflation outlook, including escalating global tariffs and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which could trigger higher imported inflation and disrupt global trade and commodity markets.

key_facts.fact: Analysts at United Capital had expected a hold, arguing the sharp rise in crude and petrol prices made a cut premature with Brent trading near $105 in mid-September.
key_facts.excerpt: "the sharp increase in crude oil and Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) prices clouds the outlook for the next quarter, making a rate cut premature." ... Global oil prices have climbed through 2026 on tensions linked to the conflict involving Iran, with Brent trading around 105 dollars a barrel in mid September.

key_facts.fact: The cut runs against the grain of developed-market policy: the Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.0% on Sept. 16, the ECB hiked 25bp on Sept. 10 and the Bank of Japan lifted its policy rate to around 1.25% on Sept. 18.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Federal Reserve on September 16 raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.0% ... On September 10, it decided to increase all three key policy rates by 25 basis points ... Japan added another leg to the tightening cycle on September 18. The Bank of Japan voted 7-2 to raise its overnight policy rate to around 1.25%.
